clue.text: Silky cloth recalled a top article from Paris

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the wordplay is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
la is a French definite article

explanation.surface: A fabric supplier brings back a French-made top from a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: A, CAP and LA together make ACAPLA, which reads backwards as ALPACA.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpaca is a soft, lustrous fabric woven from the wool of the South American animal.

clue.text: Hail charge being added to bill

indicators.note: being added to signals one piece is attached after the other

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a cost is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A surcharge is tacked onto a customer's invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' here is the verb meaning to call out to someone, not the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them, much as to hail them is to call to them.

clue.text: Group carrying off Fleet Street joke about knight

parts.note: Fleet Street was the traditional home of London's newspapers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a gag is a joke
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A gang of journalists pulling a prank involving a titled gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside GAG to give GANG. Fleet Street in London was where the British national newspapers were based.
explanation.definitionFit: A press gang was a band that seized men and carried them off for forced naval service.

clue.text: One may prepare potatoes well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a device or person that cuts potatoes into chips

explanation.surface: Someone could cook spuds properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an adverb about the cooking, but it is a separate meaning: in good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipper cuts potatoes into chips, and chipper also means bright, healthy and in good spirits.

clue.text: Book trendy holiday resort?

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
right-on means fashionably up to date in attitudes

explanation.surface: An instruction to reserve a fashionable seaside getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast; the question mark flags that it is one example of a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a famous English seaside town popular with holidaymakers, an example of the category.

clue.text: Control and rule after ousting Premier from Government

indicators.note: ousting something removes it, so the named letter is taken out

parts.note: to reign is to rule
the premier, or first, letter of the word

explanation.surface: A new leader seizes command once the Prime Minister is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' suggests a Prime Minister, but it just means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to restrain or control, and a rein is the strap used to control a horse.

clue.text: Victorian author's line supporting question in set

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits underneath the rest
one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
to ask is to question
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century writer's sentence propping up a query in a collection.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, a piece 'supporting' another is written underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth Gaskell wrote Cranford and North and South during Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Feature of steely cord?

parts.note: the doubled letter that stands out in the word: a pair, a matching couple
the letter that appears twice in the middle of steely

explanation.surface: A query about a characteristic of a cable made of strong steel.
explanation.walkthrough: The notable feature of the word steely is its doubled middle letter: a twin E. The question mark warns of this playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is a strong string made of twisted strands, a type of cord.

clue.text: No scope for this, uncovered by detective

parts.note: naked means bare, uncovered
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A sleuth reveals there is no room for manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scope' means a telescope or microscope here, not range.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing with the naked eye means using no telescope or microscope at all.

clue.text: Minister left in church, one enthralled by Catholic

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
L is the usual abbreviation for left

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive inside its grip

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clergyman quits his church after being captivated by Catholicism.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two separate insertions here, each making one half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, and a cleric is any such religious official.

clue.text: Come down and stay put, idiot!

parts.note: to dip is to drop or descend
to stick is to remain fixed in place

explanation.surface: An exasperated order to someone foolish to get down and stay still.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Someone known for pushing son is unusually pushy

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: something done unusually departs from the normal arrangement, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark about an overbearing parent who keeps pushing their boy forward.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Sisyphus was condemned to push a boulder uphill for eternity, only for it to roll back down each time.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Sisyphus is famous for endlessly rolling a rock up a hill as punishment.

clue.text: Limits to unearthing flower in a bad way

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its two ends, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
a lily is a flower

explanation.surface: There are restrictions on digging up a bloom that is in poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Uglily is the adverb of ugly, meaning in an unpleasant or nasty manner.

clue.text: Celebrity drawn to accept information

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: drawn in the sense of pulled along, as a horse is led
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A famous person is persuaded to take on some background facts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like a description of the celebrity, but it is the past participle of lead, as in led along.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a famous person, someone renowned in their field, much as a celebrity is.

clue.text: American author adopting crazy hair treatment

indicators.note: to adopt something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A US writer takes up an outlandish hairstyle product.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented ointment applied to style and slick down hair.

clue.text: I'd rally with a spoof, possibly the occasion just passed?

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be set out differently

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
more letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stage a hoax to mark the day that has just gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared just after 1 April, so the day before was the day of pranks; the spoof in the surface fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of April, traditionally a day for pranks and hoaxes, had only just passed when the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: I called out, receiving cheers in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside
out suggests being disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone shouted while being applauded, sort of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' is usually a hedge, but here it is literal: relating to a regional way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectal means relating to a dialect, a regional form of speech.

clue.text: Sufficient promotional material provided before match

indicators.note: before tells us which piece comes first in the down entry

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement
to equate is to make equal or match

explanation.surface: Enough advertising was handed out ahead of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means enough for the purpose, as sufficient does.

clue.text: What captures dramatic agile shot?

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or broken up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about what device could record a striking, nimble photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as a photograph, fitting the whole clue, but it also signals the scrambling.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital camera records images, so it is a device that captures scenes.

clue.text: Storms I encountered in equatorial weather

indicators.note: something encountered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: the trades are the trade winds that blow towards the equator
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller meets tempests in tropical conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storms' looks meteorological, but it means angry outbursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, like storms of abuse or protest.

clue.text: Back European from part of Scandinavia Germany invaded

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: a place invaded has something enter it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Norse means from Norway
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A wartime tale of a Nordic country overrun by German forces.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside NORSE, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or back a person or proposal.

clue.text: Believe censor after censor's gutted

indicators.note: after tells us which piece follows the other in the down entry
a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: only the first and last letters of the word are kept
to edit is to cut or censor material

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts a story about one censor following another who was devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' means very upset in British slang, but here it strips the word censor's to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a claim is to believe it or accept it as true.

clue.text: One's followed rivers entering coastal location

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a quay is a landing place on the shore
R is the abbreviation for river, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone is tracked as they pass waterways flowing toward the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's followed' means 'one is followed': the hunted creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarry is the prey that is being hunted or pursued by a hunter.

clue.text: Dip into detailed epic tale about love

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
placed into something means set inside it
detailed reads as de-tailed: having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: Homer's epic poem of the Trojan War
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone becomes absorbed in an intricately described romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' means de-tailed: ILIAD loses its D, giving ILIA, which is reversed with O placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise often served as a dip.

clue.text: Try to secure mark of rank, not initially for cap?

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a judge will hear or try a case

indicators.note: not initially means the opening letter is dropped from the phrase it follows

parts.note: a badge shows rank or office

explanation.surface: An attempt to fix a rank insignia that isn't the first choice for a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the courtroom sense, as a judge tries a case. A cap is one example of the answer, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear is anything worn on the head, and a cap is one such item.

clue.text: Some game much loved in radio broadcasts

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: dear means much loved

explanation.surface: A popular quiz or sport is often heard on the wireless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' here means animals hunted for food, not a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are hunted animals, and their meat, venison, is classed as game.

clue.text: Gone over first of flowers in morning moisture lots

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: ago means gone by, in the past
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
dew is the water that settles overnight

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Many blooms have passed their best in the morning wetness.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower's initial goes in after the first letter of the moisture, not at its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A good few is an idiom meaning a fairly large number, so lots.

clue.text: Telegraph's leader, probing expensive Times, rejected — not suitable for all

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the letters run the other way
a thing probing another pokes into it, so it ends up inside

parts.note: dear means costly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the paper's name
X is the multiplication or times sign

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor investigates costly rival papers and is turned away as unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper here: it is the multiplication sign. X-rated was the old British film certificate for adults only.
explanation.definitionFit: An X-rated film or show is restricted to adults, so not suitable for everyone.

clue.text: Agent's failure, coming in too soon, not leaving at the outset

indicators.note: something coming in enters another, so it sits inside it
the opening letter of leaving is taken away from the word beside it

parts.note: early means before the right time
a miss is a failure to hit

explanation.surface: A spy's blunder of arriving prematurely, rather than leaving first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not leaving at the outset' removes the first letter of the word leaving, L, not the first letter of the word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a representative sent on a mission, an agent acting on another's behalf.

clue.text: One dead-set on leaving zone frequently

indicators.note: a word leaving another is removed from it

parts.note: taken as written, before two letters go
a lot means often

explanation.surface: Someone determined to quit an area keeps trying to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: The word on leaves ZONE, giving ZE; 'One dead-set on' seems the definition, but the on belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatical person, utterly determined in pursuit of a cause.
